time.desc: The two countries launched a new round of indirect technical negotiations centered on nuclear issues and sanctions exchanges under the mediation of a third party.
The mediating party publicly stated that the two sides were close to reaching a nuclear-related agreement, and that the negotiations had a "final kick" signal.
One side and its allies launch massive joint air strikes against the other side and declare the conflict to be in open war.
The attacked party formally confirms the highest power position and completes the wartime succession arrangement.
One party issued a time-limited ultimatum to the other party, demanding the restoration of commercial shipping in key sea lanes and threatening to attack power and other civilian facilities.
One party announced that it had entered into dialogue with the other party and promised to temporarily suspend attacks on the other party's energy facilities in exchange for a window for negotiation.
One party formally submits an armistice plan containing multiple provisions to the other party to promote an end to the conflict.
The other party's formal reply to the multi-clause ceasefire plan brings the ceasefire negotiations into a new stage.
Major countries outside the region jointly proposed an alternative "five-point" plan to end the war and demanded the restoration of normal access to key sea lanes.
The leader of one side addressed the nation and announced that he would impose harsher attacks on the other side within weeks and proposed an accelerated timetable for ending the conflict.
The warring sides agreed to initiate a ceasefire lasting about two weeks to de-escalate the conflict and allow space for diplomatic negotiations
After the ceasefire came into effect, the parties openly disagreed over whether the ceasefire covered regional proxy battlefields and triggered external pressure.

One country's mainstream media revealed that its government is discussing plans to carry out military strikes on its opponent's nuclear facilities, and is evaluating expanding attacks by the end of the year to target its opponent's supreme leader.

For the first time, the side that launched the air strike publicly admitted that its soldiers were killed in the opponent's drone counterattack. The number of casualties continued to rise in the following days, breaking the "zero casualties" narrative.
The rival military launched a new missile offensive and fired missiles at an opponent's warship, while denying that it had closed the key strait.

For the first time, security figures from allies of the party that launched the air strikes admitted that the air strikes lacked a feasible plan for regime change and that the rival regime continued to exist after the attack on the leader.

The warring parties carried out air strikes on the air defense and naval facilities of the opponent's largest crude oil export hub. Multiple explosions were heard on the island, raising the risk of energy exports.

A senior financial official of a country stated his stance on shipping in the key strait, stating that he would not object to the passage of ships from some countries, and linked energy mitigation measures to the duration of the conflict.
One of the opponent's highest-ranking officials (former speaker/secretary of an agency) was killed in an allied airstrike, becoming the highest-ranking official killed since the war began.

The coalition forces participating in the war launched a new round of air strikes on the opponent's giant natural gas fields at sea. Shipping in the key strait was effectively paralyzed, and international oil and gas prices rose in response.

The opponent's military statement warned that if the opponent carried out an attack on its energy facilities, it would completely close the key strait, and the opponent threatened "unprecedented bombing" and the imposition of tariffs.
Country Y and Country Z jointly attacked Country X Region D on a dock adjacent to Strait A, resulting in several casualties.
Leader A publicly called on all countries to go to Strait A to seize oil on their own, saying that Country X had been basically defeated, and related oil prices rose sharply.
Country Y and Country Z launch joint air strikes against the City C Petrochemical Special Economic Zone in the southwest of Country X, targeting its energy infrastructure
Leader A threatens to violently bomb Country X power plants, bridges and other civilian facilities, while Country X threatens to blockade Strait B in counterattack
Country X Activities were held in various places to commemorate the slain supreme leader, and the successor supreme leader made a strong speech and proposed to collect tolls for Strait A
Country Y The Navy began to mobilize troops to Strait A and prepare to implement a blockade of the Country X port, just as the two sides were meeting in City A
Country Y The military officially launched a sea port blockade operation against Country X, investing more than 10,000 personnel and a large number of warships and aircraft
